title: /cost shows each lineage's tokens and per-model split (byModel), already computed by the read
description:
## The gap

`GET /api/proxy/issues/{identifier}/cost` gives one USD figure and one model label per lineage. It gives no tokens and no per-model split. The read already has both: the fold computes `tokens` (`lib/cost-read.js:205`) and `byModel` (`:211`), and then `workerSessions[]` is built without them (`lib/cost-read.js:472-481`; the wire shape at `:396`, and `routes/proxy-compute.js:744` strips only `telemetry`/`incomplete`).

## Why it matters

LIN-4257's research (5 Nov) found that the `model` label is the lineage's **last counted row** (`cost-read.js`, LIN-2830). All 45 implementation dispatches between 05:00 on 4 Nov and noon on 5 Nov were routed to Haiku, but `/cost` labels 21 of them Opus. In 17 of those, the Opus row is the Survey's read-only "Survey 1a" after-answer, resumed into the build session after merge. So implementation USD mixes the build with the observer, and a reader cannot:

* compare work within one model,
* separate the Survey's cost from the build's,
* or count tokens rather than dollars.

## Ask

Add to each `workerSessions[]` entry, additively:

* `tokens`: the fold's token sums (input, output, cache read, cache write);
* `byModel`: `[{ model, pricedUsd, tokens }]` from the record fold.

Snapshot-only lineages can carry `byModel: null`. Then update the `/cost` entry in the proxy instructions (`lib/proxy-instructions.js`), keeping the prompt-size budget in mind, and the cost-read tests.

Out of scope: changing the `model` label rule or the lineage attribution.

## Done when

`/cost` on a lineage with a Haiku build and an Opus follow-up shows both models, each with its USD and tokens, and the parts sum to the lineage's `costUsd`.

Filed from LIN-4257 (John's ruling, 5 Nov: write the paper read-only, and file the `/cost` change as its own ticket). The paper's v2 reads this field.

comments.body: Duplicate of LIN-4263 (filed 12:21 on 5 Nov, already In Progress), which asks for the same change: per-session model and tokens on `/cost`, with a follow-up reported as its own row. I filed this at 12:31 from the LIN-4257 ruling without seeing it. Closing as a duplicate; nothing here is lost that LIN-4263 does not already carry.

relatedIssue.title: /cost reports each session's own model and tokens (a follow-up is not the chain's model)
